summary: Kōichi Kozaka specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Hakuyu Hadano and served as a professor at Osaka Kyoiku University, where he is attested in 1991.
L. A. Ravi Varma was an Indologist who studied at Madras Medical College. Around 1938, he served as Honorary Director of the Oriental Manuscripts Department at the University of Kerala.

L. Carrington Goodrich was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Chefoo School and Williams College, and later served as Dean Lung Professor of Chinese at Columbia University from around 1945 to 1961.

L. P. N. Perera specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as head of the Post Graduate Institute of Buddhist Studies at University of Sri Lanka's Vidyalankara Campus and as Director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

Lajos Ligeti specialized in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös József Collegium, Eötvös Loránd University, and the University of Paris. In 1940, he was appointed chair of Inner Asian Studies at Eötvös Loránd University.
Lak La Sönam Chö Drub studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Lakshmanacharya was an Indologist and philosopher. He held a position at Shri Ramanuja Pathashala in Mathura, where he is attested in 1889 and attested as a teacher in 1900.

Lal Mani Joshi worked in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Allahabad, Banaras Hindu University, and Gorakhpur University under Govind Chandra Pande. He later held faculty posts at Gorakhpur and Punjabi University.
Lalchandra Bhagawandas Gandhi was an Indologist. He served as Jain Pandit at the Central Library of Baroda and held a post at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara, attested in 1939.

Lama Jampa Thaye works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a PhD at the University of Manchester, studied with several traditional teachers, and served on the international teaching faculty at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute.

Lama Kunga Rinpoche is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ngor Monastery, where he served as Thartse Shabthung in 1959. In 1973, he founded the Ewam Choden Tibetan Buddhist Center.

Lama Palden Drolma specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under traditional teachers including the 16th Karmapa, Jamgon Kongtrul the Third, Bokar Rinpoche, Situ Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, Druptop Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche, and Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche.
Lama Yeshe Gyamtso specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers Lama Norlha and Kalu Rinpoche.

Lambert Schmithausen is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar. He studied under Erich Frauwallner and Paul Hacker. He was an associate professor at the University of Münster (1970–1973) and held the Indology chair at the University of Hamburg (1973–2005).

Lance E. Nelson specializes in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctoral thesis at McMaster University by 1986 and served as a professor at the University of San Diego, where he is attested in 1997.

Lance S. Cousins worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey and Kenneth Roy Norman. He taught at Manchester (~1970–1996) and Oxford (~1996–2015), and was Pali Text Society President (2002–2003).

Lang Chen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned a PhD at Yale University, attested in 2015, under the supervision of Koichi Shinohara and Phyllis Granoff, and also studied under Janet Gyatso.

Lang Eun Ra specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Temple University, where she studied under Charles Wei-hsun Fu, Bibhuti S. Yadav, Norbert Max Samuelson, and Leonard Swidler.
Lara Braitstein specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University, where she studied under Richard P. Hayes.

Larry DeVries is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Minnesota. He taught at Minnesota, Hawaiʻi, and Washington, held a research post at Chicago, and was affiliated with Langara College in 2005.
